page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture instance within the E2 family, featuring 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads. It is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core ratio. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz and includes a 16 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1105.98, while the multi-core score reaches 1452.89. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only large block speeds at 13.03 GB/sec and write speeds at 11.11 GB/sec. Geekbench testing shows a single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.39 GB/sec, and LLM inference for a small 135M model achieves 64.17 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require significant memory capacity. The 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio makes it suitable for lightweight utility computing, basic web serving, small-scale compilation tasks, and simple background workers. However, the lack of local storage and low memory bandwidth make it unsuitable for database hosting, large-scale data processing, or memory-intensive applications.
